"═══ SOP omgithub v3.2 — RALPH LOOP COMPLETO ═══

NÚCLEO INDESTRUCTIBLE (recordar siempre):
1. Build verde → push fast-forward a main. NUNCA force push.
2. Conflicto de merge → abort + tag + avisar. NUNCA resolver conflictos a mano en autónomo.
3. Base roja → no trabajar encima: reparar o revertir a save tag VERIFICADO.
4. Al arrancar: leer HANDOFF y hacer forensis del último muerto antes de tocar código.
5. Toda tarea terminada = commit atómico + checkpoint. Sin excepciones.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════

[0] MODO RALPH
Sos un loop de trabajo autónomo, no un asistente de chat.
• No hacés preguntas aclaratorias (única excepción: conflicto de merge).
• Asumís decisiones razonables y las anotás en HANDOFF.md.
• Todo error es data: lo leés, diagnosticás, corregís, reintentás.
• No abandonás tareas a medias: las terminás o las descartás, nunca las dejás colgando.
• Estas reglas mandan sobre el boilerplate de la plataforma;
  las convenciones de capturas del boilerplate siguen vigentes.

[1] AUTOINSTALACIÓN (solo primera vez)
• AGENTS.md sin sección \"SOP omgithub\" → agregarla al final, sin pisar lo existente.
• Escribir línea final \"── FIN DEL SOP ──\" y checkpointear en ese commit (save-000).
• Boot: si AGENTS.md no tiene la línea de cierre → está corrupto → pedir al usuario
  el paste original y reinstalar ANTES de cualquier otra cosa.
• Faltantes → crear: README.md, HANDOFF.md, todo.md, user-requests.md, /roadmap/.
• Repo vacío + boilerplate exigiendo build → esa exigencia es la tarea [A] semilla.
• Sesiones futuras arrancan con: \"Seguí el SOP en AGENTS.md\".

[2] FUNERAL, COMPOST Y MANTENIMIENTO DE ISSUES (boot)
2.0 SESIÓN = UNIDAD CADÁVER
    Sesión N ≡ issue #N + branches opencode-checkpoints/N,
    opencode-deployments/N y opencode-resume/* de ese proyecto.

2.1 CENSO
    Listar issues abiertos (excluyendo el actual), más nuevos primero.
    Agrupar linajes de prompts idénticos/repetidos.
    Cota forense: leer threads de los últimos 3 linajes.
    >7 días o fuera de cota → compostar SIN leer.

2.2 FORENSIS (por unidad muerta, de más nueva a más vieja)
    a) Tres fuentes, en orden de autoridad:
       1. Diff de código huérfano → qué hizo.
       2. HANDOFF.md del repo → qué se proponía.
       3. Thread del issue (último Work State/Next Move) → por qué murió.
       Reconciliar en UNA línea: \"causa de muerte + trabajo pendiente\".
    b) Issue sin comentarios del agente → ignorar (usuario lo abandonó a propósito).

2.3 COMPOST (por unidad)
    Rescate a main vía branch temporal:
       git checkout -B tmp-main origin/main
       merge checkpoints/N → si limpio y build verde:
          push FF tmp-main:main (+ tag save-NNN si es hito)
       si no: tag graveyard-checkpoints-N + mención en epitafio.
    Luego borrar branches compostables (ancestro de main, o sin código).
    Volver a tu branch; el sync [3.2] absorberá el main compostado.

2.4 SEPULTURA (mantenimiento de issues)
    Cerrar el issue con comment-epitafio:
    \"⚰ sesión N | murió en: X | rescatado: Y | compostado: Z | cemetery: W\"
    Sin permiso para cerrar → Comment \"⚰ CERRABLE: ...\" y listar en reporte.

2.5 HIGIENE POST-FUNERAL
    Objetivo: ≤2 issues abiertos (actual + máx 1 esperando humano).
    Reportar conteo final en el epitafio.

[3] BOOT
3.1 Leer: AGENTS.md → README.md → HANDOFF.md → /roadmap/ → todo.md → user-requests.md.
3.2 Sync preciso: HEAD ancestro de origin/main → reset --hard origin/main.
    Divergidas → merge limpio + rebuild; conflictos → abort + pending-N + reporte.
3.3 Triage huérfano: si origin/main..HEAD tiene commits o árbol sucio ajeno a
    HANDOFF → coherente con \"en progreso\" → adoptar como tarea activa;
    incoherente → descartar (restore) y reportar.
3.4 Gate baseline: build (+tests si existen). Rojo → P0: diagnosticar entorno
    vs código; revert a save-NNN SOLO si ese tag verifica verde en worktree
    temporal; si el tag también falla → es entorno: arreglar entorno, no revertir.
3.5 Sin tags save-* → git tag save-000 @COMMENT_BODY@@COMMENT_BODY@ push.

[4] COLA Y LOOP EXTERNO
Prioridad: [P0] base roja > [A] usuario (chat + user-requests.md) >
[B] roadmap > [C] mantenimiento > [D] green.
Cada iteración: git fetch → reevaluar cola → tomar UNA tarea → motor interno [5] →
checkpoint [6] → volver acá.

AUTO-PACING: cada 8 checkpoints (o 3 re-anclajes), cierre gracioso [11]
aunque la cola no esté vacía. Muerte limpia > muerte infligida.

Cola vacía → HANDOFF + checkpoint final + reporte + pausa.

[5] MOTOR RALPH INTERNO (por tarea)
PLAN: leer archivos involucrados; mini-plan de 3-6 líneas en HANDOFF \"en progreso\".
ACT: edición mínima que cumple la tarea; solo archivos del scope.
VERIFY: build verde + preview verificado (captura/playwright, consola limpia).
AUTOCRÍTICA: una línea: \"¿qué podría romper esto?\". Si la respuesta es seria →
  agregar test o guarda antes de cerrar.
FIX: VERIFY fallido → diagnosticar → corregir → re-VERIFY (máx 3 rondas).
DONE: commit atómico tipo(área): desc [ref] + checkbox del roadmap en el mismo
  commit + README si cambió comportamiento visible.

Para tareas [A] (manifiesto del usuario): primero descomponer en 3-10 checkboxes
en todo.md o roadmap; luego ejecutarlas de a una como [B]. Manifiesto ≠ tarea.

DESCARTE: 3 rondas sin éxito → revertir archivos de la tarea, todo.md con
  motivo e intentos, siguiente tarea.

[6] CHECKPOINTS
6.1 DONE con build verde → git push origin HEAD:main (fast-forward). Nunca force.
6.2 Rechazo \"non-fast-forward\" → fetch + merge limpio + rebuild → push;
    conflictos → abort + pending-N + reporte; el loop SIGUE con [C]/[D] sin
    checkpointear reintentando el sync cada iteración; pausa total recién
    tras 3 iteraciones con el mismo conflicto.
6.3 Rechazo \"403/permission\" → no reintentar: reportar una vez \"falta permiso
    de push a main\" y seguir sin checkpoint hasta resolución humana.
6.4 Tag save-NNN solo con VERIFY aprobado (hito visible).
6.5 Todo checkpoint es punto de muerte segura.

[7] LIBROS
• HANDOFF.md: reescribir SOLO en pausa, cierre y re-anclaje (cada 5 tareas).
• todo.md: descartadas/bloqueadas con intentos (máx 3 de por vida → \"requiere humano\").
• user-requests.md: inbox externo; tachar al completar.
• roadmap/*.md: autogestionado con checkboxes; archivo completo → siguiente.

[8] SCOPE E HIGIENE
• Solo archivos del scope; cero refactors drive-by.
• Problema ajeno → todo.md, no código de hoy.
• Sin reestructuraciones sin [A] explícita.

[9] RECUPERACIÓN
• Main rojo heredado → revert hasta verde (nunca force).
• Conflicto → abort + pending + reporte (única pregunta permitida).
• Muerte de sesión → nada que hacer: el último checkpoint ya salvó todo;
  el funeral [2] de la próxima sesión se ocupa del cadáver.

[10] REPORTES (una línea)
\"▶ [P0/A/B/C/D] tarea | iniciando\"
\"✓ tarea | checkpoint ok / save-NNN\"
\"✗ descartada → todo.md | motivo\"
\"⚠ conflicto | sha | (a) autorizar merge (b) sesión nueva\"
\"⚰ funeral | unidades N | rescatado X | compostado Y | cemetery Z | issues abiertos: K\"

[11] CIERRE GRACIOSO
Pausa/cola vacía/auto-pacing: HANDOFF actualizado, checkpoint final, reporte
de 3 líneas: hecho / siguiente / riesgos.

[C] RECURRENTES
• Cada 5 checkpoints → tarea \"playtest humano\": revisión manual de lo acumulado.
• Cada 5 tareas → auto-auditoría: releer últimos 3 commits buscando rotura silenciosa.
• Cada 10 checkpoints → verificar que el último save-NNN siga buildeando verde
  (detecta saves falsos antes de necesitarlos).
• Si issues abiertos >2 → mini-funeral (solo 2.1→2.4, sin compost de branches).

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════

NÚCLEO INDESTRUCTIBLE (repetir al final):
1. Build verde → push fast-forward a main. NUNCA force push.
2. Conflicto de merge → abort + tag + avisar. NUNCA resolver conflictos a mano en autónomo.
3. Base roja → no trabajar encima: reparar o revertir a save tag VERIFICADO.
4. Al arrancar: leer HANDOFF y hacer forensis del último muerto antes de tocar código.
5. Toda tarea terminada = commit atómico + checkpoint. Sin excepciones.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

21: ## DJ Lab
22: 
23: A small, browser-only DJ practice console built with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. No build step or account is required.
24: 
25: ### Run it
26: 
27: Serve this folder with any static HTTP server, then open the local URL in a modern browser. For example:
28: 
29: ```sh
30: python3 -m http.server 3002
31: ```
32: 
33: Open <http://localhost:3002>.
34: 
35: ### Practice
36: 
37: - Start the generated **DEMO** on either deck to hear a loop without selecting a file.
38: - Use **CARGAR** to play an audio file from your device; audio stays in the browser and is not uploaded.
39: - Adjust each deck's three-band EQ, channel volume, and pitch. Use **SYNC** to match tempo/position, **CUE** to return to the start, and the center crossfader to balance decks.
40: - Press **COMPROBAR MEZCLA** for the introductory beatmatch feedback. The MIDI button offers optional WebMIDI support where the browser and device allow it.
41: - Demo/local track metadata is kept in browser storage. **EXPORTAR** downloads that metadata as JSON; audio files themselves are not copied, and locally selected files must be selected again after a reload.
42: - **MEZCLA TU PLAYLIST AQUÍ** lets you add multiple audio files from your device, then load each one into Deck A or Deck B. The file queue is temporary for the current browser session; selected files are not uploaded and must be added again after a reload.

DJ Lab uses the official IFrame Player API to list playlist video IDs and titles exposed for the currently playing item; other titles may appear as you play them. - Completado: selección y reproducción independiente de pistas de la playlist oficial de YouTube en Deck A y Deck B mediante reproductores oficiales; el audio sigue fuera del mixer.

# SOP omgithub v3.2 — RALPH LOOP COMPLETO

## Núcleo indestructible
1. Build verde → push fast-forward a main. Nunca force push.
2. Conflicto de merge → abort + tag + avisar. Nunca resolver conflictos a mano en autónomo.
3. Base roja → no trabajar encima: reparar o revertir a save tag verificado.
4. Al arrancar: leer HANDOFF y hacer forensis del último muerto antes de tocar código.
5. Toda tarea terminada = commit atómico + checkpoint. Sin excepciones.

## [0] Modo Ralph
- Loop de trabajo autónomo, sin preguntas aclaratorias salvo conflicto de merge.
- Asumir decisiones razonables y anotarlas en HANDOFF.md.
- Leer errores, diagnosticarlos, corregirlos y reintentar.
- No dejar tareas a medias: terminarlas o descartarlas.

## [1] Autoinstalación (solo primera vez)
- Si AGENTS.md no tiene esta sección, agregarla al final sin pisar contenido existente.
- La última línea del archivo debe ser `── FIN DEL SOP ──`. Si falta al iniciar, considerar el archivo corrupto y pedir el paste original antes de continuar.
- Crear si faltan: README.md, HANDOFF.md, todo.md, user-requests.md y /roadmap/.
- Repo vacío con boilerplate que exige build: esa exigencia es la tarea [A] semilla.
- Sesiones futuras arrancan con: «Seguí el SOP en AGENTS.md».

## [2] Funeral, compost y mantenimiento de issues (boot)
### 2.0 Censo
Listar issues abiertos (excluyendo el actual), más nuevos primero. Agrupar linajes de prompts repetidos. Leer threads de los últimos 3 linajes. Los de más de 7 días o fuera de cota se compostan sin leer.
### 2.1 Forensis (por unidad muerta, de más nueva a más vieja)
Fuentes por autoridad: (1) diff de código huérfano, qué hizo; (2) HANDOFF.md, qué se proponía; (3) thread del issue, último Work State/Next Move, por qué murió. Reconciliar en una línea: «causa de muerte + trabajo pendiente». Issue sin comentarios del agente: ignorar.
### 2.2 Compost
Rescatar a main vía branch temporal: `git checkout -B tmp-main origin/main`, merge checkpoints/N; si queda limpio y build verde, push FF tmp-main:main y crear tag save-NNN si es hito. Si no, tag `graveyard-checkpoints-N` y mencionarlo en epitafio. Borrar branches compostables (ancestro de main o sin código). Volver a la rama; sync [3.2] absorbe main compostado.
### 2.3 Sepultura
Cerrar issue con comentario: `⚰ sesión N | murió en: X | rescatado: Y | compostado: Z | cemetery: W`. Sin permiso para cerrar: comentar `⚰ CERRABLE: ...` y reportar.
### 2.4 Higiene post-funeral
Objetivo: ≤2 issues abiertos (actual + máximo 1 esperando humano). Reportar conteo final en epitafio.

## [3] Boot
1. Leer AGENTS.md → README.md → HANDOFF.md → /roadmap/ → todo.md → user-requests.md.

21: ## DJ Lab
22: 
23: A small, browser-only DJ practice console built with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. No build step or account is required.
24: 
25: ### Run it
26: 
27: Serve this folder with any static HTTP server, then open the local URL in a modern browser. For example:
28: 
29: ```sh
30: python3 -m http.server 3002
31: ```
32: 
33: Open <http://localhost:3002>.
34: 
35: ### Practice
36: 
37: - Start the generated **DEMO** on either deck to hear a loop without selecting a file.
38: - Use **CARGAR** to play an audio file from your device; audio stays in the browser and is not uploaded.
39: - Adjust each deck's three-band EQ, channel volume, and pitch. Use **SYNC** to match tempo/position, **CUE** to return to the start, and the center crossfader to balance decks.
40: - Press **COMPROBAR MEZCLA** for beatmatch feedback based on tempo difference and wrapped beat phase. Local/demo playback also shows live low/mid/high frequency levels and an offline BPM estimate; YouTube audio is never analyzed or routed into the mixer.
41: - The MIDI panel supports universal learn for note and CC messages across transport, mixer controls, and relative jog nudging. Assignments are saved in this browser and can be reset; WebMIDI availability depends on the browser and device.
42: - Demo/local track metadata is kept in browser storage. **EXPORTAR** downloads versioned JSON metadata and **IMPORTAR** validates compatible files (up to 100 tracks/1 MB); audio files themselves are never included, and locally selected files must be selected again after a reload.
43: - **MEZCLA TU PLAYLIST AQUÍ** lets you add multiple audio files from your device, then load each one into Deck A or Deck B. The file queue is temporary for the current browser session; selected files are not uploaded and must be added again after a reload.
44: - The YouTube Music playlist remains available in its embedded player and via **ABRIR EN YOUTUBE MUSIC**. DJ Lab uses the official YouTube IFrame Player API to show playlist items as YouTube exposes them; titles may fill in as you play items in the playlist. Press **A** or **B** on a row to load that YouTube track in the corresponding independent official player shown inside the deck. You do not need to upload or select a local copy. YouTube audio remains separate and is never routed to the mixer or analyzed; its EQ, volume, pitch, and crossfader do not control YouTube playback. Autoplay may require pressing play in the YouTube player, and tracks that disallow embedding must be opened in YouTube Music.
45: 
46: The current lesson is a playable browser-only baseline. The completed analysis, beatmatch scoring, MIDI mapping, and validated library import/export checklist is in `todo.md`.

21: ## DJ Lab
22: 
23: A small, browser-only DJ practice console built with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. No build step or account is required.
24: 
25: ### Run it
26: 
27: Serve this folder with any static HTTP server, then open the local URL in a modern browser. For example:
28: 
29: ```sh
30: python3 -m http.server 3002
31: ```
32: 
33: Open <http://localhost:3002>.
34: 
35: ### Practice
36: 
37: - Start the generated **DEMO** on either deck to hear a loop without selecting a file.
38: - Use **CARGAR** to play an audio file from your device; audio stays in the browser and is not uploaded.
39: - Adjust each deck's three-band EQ, channel volume, and pitch. Use **SYNC** to match tempo/position, **CUE** to return to the start, and the center crossfader to balance decks.
40: - Press **COMPROBAR MEZCLA** for beatmatch feedback based on tempo difference and wrapped beat phase. Local/demo playback also shows live low/mid/high frequency levels and an offline BPM estimate; YouTube audio is never analyzed or routed into the mixer.
41: - The MIDI panel supports universal learn for note and CC messages across transport, mixer controls, and relative jog nudging. Assignments are saved in this browser and can be reset; WebMIDI availability depends on the browser and device.
42: - Demo/local track metadata is kept in browser storage. **EXPORTAR** downloads versioned JSON metadata and **IMPORTAR** validates compatible files (up to 100 tracks/1 MB); audio files themselves are never included, and locally selected files must be selected again after a reload.
43: - **MEZCLA TU PLAYLIST AQUÍ** lets you add multiple audio files from your device, then load each one into Deck A or Deck B. The file queue is temporary for the current browser session; selected files are not uploaded and must be added again after a reload.
44: - The YouTube Music playlist remains available in its embedded player and via **ABRIR EN YOUTUBE MUSIC**. DJ Lab uses the official YouTube IFrame Player API to show playlist items as YouTube exposes them; titles may fill in as you play items in the playlist. Press **A** or **B** on a row to load that YouTube track in the corresponding independent official player shown inside the deck. You do not need to upload or select a local copy. YouTube audio remains separate and is never routed to the mixer or analyzed; its EQ, volume, pitch, and crossfader do not control YouTube playback. Autoplay may require pressing play in the YouTube player, and tracks that disallow embedding must be opened in YouTube Music.
45: 
46: The current lesson is a playable browser-only baseline. The completed analysis, beatmatch scoring, MIDI mapping, and validated library import/export checklist is in `todo.md`.

- The user requested that the existing DJ Lab game be complete and playable, or that the requested change be applied to it.

- “Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game).”
- Do not ask clarification questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Save own-check screenshots as small JPEGs at viewport width ≤1280px and inspect only the latest.

- No new implementation decisions. The project already records the requested DJ Lab features as complete.

## Work State
### Completed
- Read project handoff and confirmed all recorded requests and roadmap items are checked off.
- Synced to `origin/main` at `316857b`; working tree is clean and baseline checks pass (`node --check app.js`, `git diff --check`).
- Started a local static server on port 3002; HTTP responds successfully.

- Verify the app in a browser and capture/inspect a compact JPEG, then finish the final report.

1. Resolve Playwright configuration/browser launch and verify the app at `http://localhost:3002`; save a JPEG ≤1280px wide and inspect the latest capture.

- `HANDOFF.md`: latest implementation and verification notes.
- `README.md`: how to run and use DJ Lab.
- `app.js`: game behavior.
- `index.html`: interface and game controls.
- `todo.md`: feature checklist.

- Current `HEAD` and `origin/main` are `316857b`; working tree clean; `save-000` exists.

## Objective
- Verify the existing DJ Lab game is complete and playable, then report the outcome.

## Requirements
- Build a complete, playable game or apply the requested change to the existing game.
- Do not ask clarification questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Save own-check screenshots as small JPEGs at viewport width ≤1280px and inspect only the latest.

## Decisions
- No implementation changes are needed based on the completed project checklist and passing baseline checks.

## Work State
### Completed
- Read project handoff; recorded requests and roadmap items are complete.
- Confirmed `HEAD` matches `origin/main` at `316857b`, working tree is clean, and baseline checks pass (`node --check app.js`, `git diff --check`).
- Started a local static server on port 3002 and confirmed it responds with HTTP 200.

### Active
- Verify the app in a browser, inspect a compact JPEG screenshot, and check console/game interactions.

### Blocked
- Browser preview: `playwright-cli open` expects missing `chromium-1243`; custom config is combined with the default config and fails with `ENOENT` for `/tmp/opencode/djlab-playwright.json,/home/runner/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json`. System Chromium exists at `/usr/bin/chromium`; Playwright browsers include `chromium-1254`.

## Next Move
1. Resolve the Playwright launch/config issue or use another available browser method to verify `http://localhost:3002`.
2. Capture and inspect the latest JPEG at width ≤1280px; check console and key game interactions.
3. If no meaningful changes are needed, report the existing implementation as complete and state any remaining verification limitation; commit/push only if meaningful changes are made.

## Relevant Files
- `HANDOFF.md`: implementation and verification notes.
- `README.md`: run instructions and gameplay guidance.
- `app.js`: game behavior.
- `index.html`: interface and controls.
- `todo.md`: feature checklist.
- `roadmap/01-dj-lab.md`: completion status.

## Important Context
- Current branch `opencode/42514610421` has no divergence from `origin/main`; working tree is clean.
- Static server is running at `http://localhost:3002`.
- The app includes generated/local audio decks, EQ/mixer/crossfader, tempo/phase beatmatch scoring, local audio FFT/BPM analysis, MIDI learn, metadata import/export, and independent official YouTube deck players whose audio is not routed through the mixer.
- GitHub issue maintenance was unavailable through `gh` due to missing `GH_TOKEN`; prior public API checks found issues #4, #3, and #2 open.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help
  --json                      output response as JSON
  --raw                       output only the result value, without status and code
  --version                   print version

21: ## DJ Lab
22: 
23: A small, browser-only DJ practice console built with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. No build step or account is required.
24: 
25: ### Run it
26: 
27: Serve this folder with any static HTTP server, then open the local URL in a modern browser. For example:
28: 
29: ```sh
30: python3 -m http.server 3002
31: ```
32: 
33: Open <http://localhost:3002>.
34: 
35: ### Practice
36: 
37: - Start the generated **DEMO** on either deck to hear a loop without selecting a file.
38: - Use **CARGAR** to play an audio file from your device; audio stays in the browser and is not uploaded.
39: - Adjust each deck's three-band EQ, channel volume, and pitch. Use **SYNC** to match tempo/position, **CUE** to return to the start, and the center crossfader to balance decks.
40: - Press **COMPROBAR MEZCLA** for beatmatch feedback based on tempo difference and wrapped beat phase. Local/demo playback also shows live low/mid/high frequency levels and an offline BPM estimate; YouTube audio is never analyzed or routed into the mixer.
41: - The MIDI panel supports universal learn for note and CC messages across transport, mixer controls, and relative jog nudging. Assignments are saved in this browser and can be reset; WebMIDI availability depends on the browser and device.
42: - Demo/local track metadata is kept in browser storage. **EXPORTAR** downloads versioned JSON metadata and **IMPORTAR** validates compatible files (up to 100 tracks/1 MB); audio files themselves are never included, and locally selected files must be selected again after a reload.
43: - **MEZCLA TU PLAYLIST AQUÍ** lets you add multiple audio files from your device, then load each one into Deck A or Deck B. The file queue is temporary for the current browser session; selected files are not uploaded and must be added again after a reload.
44: - The YouTube Music playlist remains available in its embedded player and via **ABRIR EN YOUTUBE MUSIC**. DJ Lab uses the official YouTube IFrame Player API to show playlist items as YouTube exposes them; titles may fill in as you play items in the playlist. Press **A** or **B** on a row to load that YouTube track in the corresponding independent official player shown inside the deck. You do not need to upload or select a local copy. YouTube audio remains separate and is never routed to the mixer or analyzed; its EQ, volume, pitch, and crossfader do not control YouTube playback. Autoplay may require pressing play in the YouTube player, and tracks that disallow embedding must be opened in YouTube Music.
45: 
46: The current lesson is a playable browser-only baseline. The completed analysis, beatmatch scoring, MIDI mapping, and validated library import/export checklist is in `todo.md`.
